I got this "Olivio Coconut Oil Spread". Picked it up in a hurry not paying attention.

It contains "Extra Virgin Coconut, Sustainable Palm Fruit, Canola" - and is non-hydrogenated.

I'm not up on all my oils. I know a lot of those vegetable oils are terrible for you. But I'm not sure about this particular product.

Absolute garbage or worth using until I go shopping next?

I try and avoid products with palm and canola oils. Depending on how much you're going to be using and how much vegetable oil you consume besides this product, it's probably not a huge deal. I wouldn't buy it again. I don't think it's something you absolutely can't use. If you haven't opened it, and could still return it, I might avoid using it and get my money back. If it's open, just use it.
Well I bought 3 of them cuz they were fairly cheap (like 3 bucks each). I tried one and it's fairly tasty.

Well, if you like it, then eat it. I'm not sure canola oil is great for health, but it's probably tolerable in moderation. I oppose palm oils mainly from a sustainability concern (the palm oil here may have been sustainably grown but buying products with palm oil only demonstrates a market for it that helps drive the unsustainable production). What's done is done.
What's actually wrong with canola oil, other than everyone upset over "GMO"?

It's not about GMO at all. It's about the amount of Omega-6 fatty acids found in canola (and other vegetable oils) along with links to inflammation and some potential links to some cancers. Granted, other studies say it might be beneficial against other cancers. The jury is still out on that. Even the unhydrogenated canola oils have trans-fats in them (from 0.56%-4.2%).

In the end, it's just not a food product that I, personally, think is worth the benefit of the doubt. Especially when there are so many delicious animal fats out there. I would much rather have some butter.
